platform.title: Platform, identity, billing, admin and developer surface
platform.why: Everything that defines who a user is, which workspace/plan they are on, what they pay, how admins run the platform and how outsiders integrate. Shares one data spine (users, workspaces, plans, wallet) and the kernel work (skeleton PR, web shell, operator layer), so one person owning it avoids the most cross-talk.

messaging.title: WhatsApp core, inbox and automation
messaging.why: The WhatsApp connection engines, the Node bridge, chat, team inbox, broadcasts, campaigns, templates, auto-reply and the flow builder/runtime all read and write the same conversation, message and queue tables and share the channel core, so they must move together.

crm.title: CRM, commerce, AI and the other channels
crm.why: Contacts and the sales objects around them (deals, companies, tasks, proposals, invoices, appointments), the commerce stack (catalog, storefront, checkout, shop integrations), AI agents and the nine non-WhatsApp channel adapters. The channels are siblings of one adapter pattern, so one person builds them consistently once the channel core exists.

foundation.title: Skeleton PR: per-domain shells, generated registries, timestamp migrations, decorator registries, per-domain docs (conflict-map section 2)
Web foundation: app shells, @crm/ui, session/BFF, API client, i18n with RTL, nav registry
Operator layer: super-admin actor kind, workspace signup/onboarding, plan and limit gating hook (decisions for D4, D5)
Channel core: channels table and credential vault, provider ports, ingest pipeline, unified message model
Worker plumbing: queue registry, outbox subscribers, realtime bridge (redis-emitter)
Storage and mail: S3 client, uploads with quota and MIME checks, signed URLs, mailer
Test harness and CI: API e2e harness, web e2e, CI jobs for web
